$comment: Coverage universe. `ticker` drives EDGAR lookup for financials+citations. layer/segment/verticals/moat are analyst judgment and are authored, not scraped. is_public=false means no filings exist and figures must come from press with is_estimate=true.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.note: Gas turbine slots sold out into the 2030s; >$2B data-center electrification orders in 2025, ~3x prior year.

companies.name: Cummins
companies.note: Standby gensets for data centers; diversified into trucking so AI is a minority exposure.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.note: Solid-oxide fuel cells sited behind the meter — bypasses interconnect queues, which is the real constraint.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.note: Largest US nuclear fleet; Three Mile Island restart for Microsoft. Existing nuclear is the only carbon-free firm power available this decade.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.note: Nuclear plus a large gas fleet — the flexible capacity that can actually be added on AI timelines.

companies.name: Cameco
companies.note: Uranium upstream. Levered to the nuclear narrative more than to near-term AI megawatts.

companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.note: Largest US renewables developer; PPAs and co-located generation for hyperscalers.

companies.name: Talen Energy
companies.note: Susquehanna nuclear co-location with AWS — the template deal for behind-the-meter data centers.

companies.name: Dominion Energy
companies.note: Northern Virginia — the densest data-center corridor on earth. Interconnect queue is the bottleneck.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.note: Liquid cooling and thermal management. Organic orders +81%; rack density is gated by heat rejection.

companies.name: Modine Manufacturing
companies.note: Data-center cooling is the growth segment inside a legacy thermal business.

companies.name: Trane Technologies
companies.note: Applied HVAC scaled to campus-level thermal loads.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.note: Switchgear, UPS, busway. Transformer and switchgear lead times are a hard physical gate on energization.

companies.name: Hubbell
companies.note: Grid and utility electrical equipment; levered to substation build.

companies.name: Quanta Services
companies.note: Transmission and substation construction. Skilled-labor constrained, which caps how fast capex converts to megawatts.

companies.name: EMCOR Group
companies.note: Mechanical/electrical contracting for data center fit-out.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.note: ~92% of revenue is Data Center. Sells full NVL racks, not just chips — the layer boundary is genuinely blurred. CUDA is the switching cost.

companies.name: AMD
companies.note: The only credible merchant GPU alternative; software ecosystem is the gap.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.note: Custom ASICs for Google TPU and other hyperscaler silicon, plus Tomahawk switching. The pick-and-shovel play on hyperscalers escaping NVDA.

companies.name: Marvell
companies.note: Custom silicon and optical DSPs; smaller ASIC franchise than AVGO.

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.note: CPU IP licensing; royalty model means it monetizes unit volume regardless of who wins.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.note: HBM output sold out through 2026. Memory bandwidth, not FLOPs, bounds inference economics.

companies.name: SanDisk
companies.note: NAND supply into AI storage tiers amid severe pricing upcycle.

companies.name: Seagate
companies.note: Nearline HDD for the data lakes feeding training. Quietly tight supply.

companies.name: ASML
companies.note: Monopoly on EUV. The single narrowest chokepoint in the entire stack — no substitute exists at any price.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.note: Deposition and etch breadth; levered to leading-edge and HBM capacity adds.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.note: Etch and deposition; high-aspect-ratio NAND and HBM TSV exposure.

companies.name: KLA Corporation
companies.note: Process control near-monopoly; yield matters more as nodes shrink.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.note: Manufactures essentially every leading-edge AI accelerator. CoWoS advanced packaging is the acknowledged industry bottleneck; N3 running above 100% utilization. Also the largest single geopolitical concentration risk in the stack.

companies.name: Intel
companies.note: Foundry ambitions plus US government stake; the only Western leading-edge alternative if it executes.

companies.name: GlobalFoundries
companies.note: Mature-node specialty; not leading-edge AI logic.

companies.name: Entegris
companies.note: Advanced materials and contamination control; consumable, so it tracks wafer starts not capex.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.note: OSAT packaging — the partner capacity TSMC leans on to relieve CoWoS.

companies.name: MKS Instruments
companies.note: Subsystems and process chemistry into semicap tools.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.note: Ethernet switching for AI back-end fabrics; the Ethernet-vs-InfiniBand share shift is the debate.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.note: Optical transceivers; 800G/1.6T ramp is directly levered to cluster scale-out.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.note: PCIe/CXL connectivity silicon — scale-up inside the rack rather than between racks.

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.note: Active electrical cables and SerDes; high customer concentration.

companies.name: Ciena
companies.note: DCI optical transport as training spans multiple sites.

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.note: AI server backlog is large but gross margin is thin — integration is a pass-through business.

companies.name: Super Micro Computer
companies.note: Fast to market on new GPU platforms; margin compression and governance history are the bear case.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.note: ODM for hyperscaler custom racks and switches; benefits from white-box share gain.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
companies.note: AI systems plus Juniper networking; enterprise rather than hyperscale weighted.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.note: $104B backlog against heavy debt; capex ran ~3x revenue in Q2 2026. Microsoft concentration ~62% in 2024, de-risking via Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic.

companies.name: Nebius Group
companies.note: European neocloud; post-Yandex restructuring.

companies.name: IREN
companies.note: Bitcoin miner converting powered shells to GPU cloud — the energy asset is the moat, not the compute.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.note: Interconnection density is the moat; AI training is less interconnection-intensive than enterprise colo.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.note: Hyperscale wholesale capacity; pre-leasing rates and power banked are the metrics.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.note: Azure plus the OpenAI relationship plus Copilot. Spans three layers; primary placement is hyperscale.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.note: Only player owning the full stack — TPU silicon, DCs, frontier models, distribution. Printed first negative FCF since 2004 IPO on capex.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.note: AWS plus Trainium/Inferentia silicon plus the Anthropic stake.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.note: Capex without a cloud rental business to monetize it — the purest capex-vs-return test case.

companies.name: Oracle
companies.note: RPO exploded on OpenAI commitments; the debate is customer concentration and financing of the build.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.note: ~$40B annualized as of Aug 2026, up from ~$20B at end-2025. Private: all figures are press-reported estimates.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.note: ~$65B run-rate end-July 2026, having passed OpenAI. Went ~$9B (end-2025) to $47B (May) to $65B (Jul). Enterprise/API weighted.

companies.name: xAI
companies.note: Colossus cluster; vertically integrated with its own power generation.

companies.name: Snowflake
companies.note: Enterprise data gravity is the moat; consumption model means AI workloads show up in revenue directly.

companies.name: MongoDB
companies.note: Vector search inside the operational database — bundling against standalone vector DBs.

companies.name: Datadog
companies.note: LLM observability attach; AI-native customers are a visible cohort in its own disclosures.

companies.name: Databricks
companies.note: Private. Lakehouse plus MosaicML; the main Snowflake counterweight.

companies.name: Reddit
companies.note: Human-generated corpus under license to Google and OpenAI. Data licensing is high-margin and contractual.

companies.name: Thomson Reuters
companies.note: Proprietary legal corpus; won the Ross Intelligence copyright case, which set the tone for training-data litigation.

companies.name: RELX
companies.note: Scientific and legal corpora; LexisNexis and Elsevier are rivalrous training data.

companies.name: AppLovin
companies.note: ML-driven ad targeting — AI as the product engine rather than a feature.

companies.name: Netflix
companies.note: Recommendation and production tooling; AI is margin support, not a revenue line.

companies.name: CrowdStrike
companies.note: Telemetry scale is the data moat; agentic SOC is the expansion vector.

companies.name: Palo Alto Networks
companies.note: Platformization plus AI security posture management.

companies.name: Cloudflare
companies.note: Edge inference plus the pay-per-crawl stance on AI scrapers — a rare toll on training data.

companies.name: ServiceNow
companies.note: Workflow system of record; agentic AI upsell into an installed base with real switching costs.

companies.name: Salesforce
companies.note: Agentforce monetization is the key debate — seat model versus consumption as agents replace seats.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.note: Ontology plus government entrenchment; valuation is the entire bear case.

companies.name: Anysphere (Cursor)
companies.note: Private. Fastest-scaling AI-native developer tool; gross margin depends entirely on model input costs it does not control.

companies.name: Tempus AI
companies.note: Multimodal clinical-genomic data; the data asset is the moat, diagnostics is the wedge.

companies.name: Veeva Systems
companies.note: Life-sciences system of record; regulated workflows are extremely sticky.

companies.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
companies.note: AI-first drug discovery; the thesis rests on clinical readouts, not software metrics.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.note: Real-world video data flywheel plus Dojo/AI5 silicon; autonomy and Optimus are the AI-levered pieces.

companies.name: Mobileye
companies.note: ADAS silicon and stack; design-win cycles are long and OEM-dependent.

companies.name: Symbotic
companies.note: Warehouse automation with heavy Walmart concentration — a textbook customer-concentration case.
